turns.text: Good to see you both. Desmond, Dad. Dad, the log is mostly what you did, which is actually really useful. I'd like to fill in Desmond's side with him today. Let's start with mornings.
Yeah, mornings are the main thing. I've been driving him every day. We leave before seven. Some days we're there half an hour before the doors open.
Desmond, what's it like for you in the car on the way?
I just watch the clock. If the bridge is bad I start doing the math, like if we're going to make it.
And what's the worst part about being late? What do you picture?
Opening the door to homeroom and everybody turns around. Like everyone stops and looks at you. And Mr. Hale says something.
Everyone turns around and stares. That's a hard picture. On the zero to ten, how big is the worry on a morning where it looks like you might be late?
Eight. If we're actually late, more.
Eight. Thank you. Dad, on the sixth you wrote that you called the office and took him in at second period. Can you tell me about that?
We were maybe four minutes late. He wouldn't get out. I didn't want a fight, so I called and said he'd be in for second.
Desmond, waiting until second period, what did that do to the worry?
It went away. Because second period nobody's late, everyone's just walking in.
Right. So the worry goes away fast, but you missed homeroom and first period to make it go away. And the next morning the worry wants to leave even earlier. Is that fair?
I guess. Yeah.
Now, there's another thing in here that sounds a bit similar but I don't think it's the same. Soccer pickup. Dad, you wrote nine texts in fifteen minutes.
That one's different. That's when I'm waiting for him. I answer every single one. I've started leaving work early so I'm there first.
Desmond, when you're waiting at practice and Dad's not there yet, what's the worry?
That something happened. Like a crash or something. Because he's never late, so if he's late something's wrong.

So with mornings it's I'll be late and people will stare. With pickup it's Dad is late and something bad happened to him. Both are about being late, but they're really different worries. How big is the pickup one?
Six. It's less. Once he texts back it's fine.
Six. And then it comes back after a few minutes and you text again?
Yeah.
Okay. Dad, one more thing. The school counselor called about the day there was a fire drill and he got to math late.
She said he was checked out all afternoon. I asked him and he said nothing happened.
Desmond, anything you want to say about that afternoon?
Not really. I was just tired.
Okay. We'll leave that as a question for now. I also saw the note about the backpack. You carry everything so you don't stop at your locker?
If I go to my locker I'm late to science. It's on the other side.
Have you ever actually been late to science from going to your locker?
I don't know. I haven't tried it.

That's a really honest answer. We don't know yet, because the worry hasn't let you test it. Okay. Let me suggest a few things and you tell me if they're fair. Desmond, you said on the thirteenth you wanted to take the bus like your friend.
Yeah but then I didn't.
Could you take the bus two mornings this week? The bus gets there on time, but not thirty minutes early. That's the practice: arriving at a normal time.
Two days. Can I pick which ones?
You can pick. Tell Dad tonight which two. Dad, on the days he drives with you, can you leave at your normal time, seven twenty-five, not before seven?
I can do that. I'd honestly like my mornings back.
And for pickup, I'd like you to send one text when you leave work, and then not answer the follow-up texts. Desmond, you'll know he's on his way from that one text.
What if he's really late?
If he's more than fifteen minutes past the time he said, you can call once. That's the deal. Dad, okay?
Okay.

Good. So: Desmond takes the bus two mornings, his choice which. On drive days Dad leaves at seven twenty-five. For pickup, Dad sends one text when he leaves and doesn't reply to follow-ups; Desmond can call once if Dad is fifteen minutes past. We're not doing anything with the locker yet. Dad, keep logging, and when you can, add a line about what Desmond did, not just what you did.
